Subject: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up - ACME

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have a shared checklist before the test window: 

Recap (agreed on call)
- Target end-to-end API latency: p95 <= 200ms for non-streaming requests; streaming tail latency target <= 250ms
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline 120 req/s sustained, spike to 250 req/s; concurrent streaming sessions ~200 (with 50 sustained active concurrently)
- Internal network budget: request path inside ACME VPC + egress to Redwood should target <= 50ms median; anything consistently >100ms will need troubleshooting
- TLS: please confirm where TLS terminates (ALB/NLB) and whether we can accept connections to a dedicated IP for testing

What we need from ACME before the test window:
1) Network diagram (VPCs, Transit Gateway, VPN/DirectConnect, NAT/egress path) — you mentioned a diagram; please attach
2) Confirmation of TLS termination (ALB / NLB) and whether you can open an outbound test to a Redwood test endpoint
3) A preferred 2-hour test window (we suggested Nov 6 or Nov 9) and point person for network ops

Next steps from our side:
- Jordan will send a short test plan (iperf + curl tests + streaming probe) and a temporary test endpoint + expected metrics to capture
- We'll provision a dedicated test endpoint on our private deployment in us-west-2 to minimize cross-region noise

Attachments: please attach your network diagram if possible.

Thanks — look forward to running tests and validating the SLOs.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the recap. Attaching the VPC diagram (acme_vpc_network_diagram.pdf). A few quick answers: 

- We have an AWS setup in us-west-2. Traffic from our app fleet goes through an ALB where TLS is terminated, then to an internal NLB for service routing. Egress to external services goes through NAT Gateways in the same region.
- We peer our VPCs via Transit Gateway; we also have an IPSEC VPN tunnel to our on-prem datacenter for critical workloads.
- Our internal latency between app subnets and NAT is typically 15–35ms (measured historically), but we can run tests to get exact RTTs to your endpoint.

We can provision access for outbound tests to a Redwood test IP. Nov 6 between 09:00–11:00 PST works for our network team. Priya will be the lead on our side.

Tom

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up - ACME
Attachments: redwood_private_sizing.xlsx

Thanks Tom — diagram received, looks good. Adding a short test plan and a few network questions so ACME knows what we'll run during the Nov 6 window.

Test plan (high level)
1) Baseline TCP RTTs: run traceroute and 10 x ping series from app subnet to Redwood test endpoint
2) Bandwidth / jitter: iperf3 bi-directional (5x 30s runs) to estimate throughput and jitter under no load and with simulated application load
3) TLS path validation: curl requests to API endpoint (non-streaming) to measure full handshake + first-byte latency (we'll send a small payload series of 100 requests at 1 RPS then ramp)
4) Streaming probe: open persistent streaming connections (WebSocket / SSE) up to 200 concurrent clients to measure tail latency and connection stability; capture p95/p99 for token/event delivery
5) Application-level throughput test: spike testing to 250 req/s for short bursts while monitoring p50/p95/p99 latencies

Questions / asks for ACME
- Can you run iperf3 from both app-subnet (ECS/EKS workers) and from on-prem through the VPN?
- Are there any NAT gateway or proxy rate limits we should be aware of?
- Please confirm whether your ALB injects any additional headers or does TLS offload with client IP preserved (we prefer X-Forwarded-For present)

Operational notes
- We'll provide a temporary, single-purpose IP and hostname for the test to minimize DNS caching effects
- Jordan recommends opening ephemeral firewall rules for the test timeframe; we will provide the exact ports (iperf3 default, TCP/443 for API tests, and WS/SSE ports if different)

I've attached a quick sizing workbook (redwood_private_sizing.xlsx) that maps request shapes to expected GPU sizing and concurrent capacity so ACME can validate internal capacity planning post-demo.

Marissa — please confirm Nov 6 09:00–11:00 PST with ACME and that Priya will be the on-call for any network troubleshooting.

-jordan
Jordan Blake
Infra Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up - ACME

Hi all — thanks for the plan and the sizing workbook. Confirming Nov 6 09:00–11:00 PST for the network tests. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- TLS termination: TLS is terminated at the ALB (client certs not in use). We can preserve X-Forwarded-For.
- NAT limits: no explicit rate limits on our NAT gateways but our egress goes through a pair of NAT gateways with around 10Gbps combined; we do have guardrails in our WAF for suspicious patterns (we will whitelist the test endpoint).
- We can run iperf3 from our on-prem through the IPSEC tunnel and from an EKS worker in the app VPC. We'll send an internal contact for the test run (network ops pager) prior to the window.

Looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Priya Singh
Senior Network Engineer | Acme Corp
